name: Battery C, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA) / 62nd AAA Gun Bn
note: 1st Bn, 62nd CA (AA) became the 62nd AAA Gun Bn at Palermo; the battery's own reports switch name between Mar and Apr 1944. A gun battery (its embarkation roster of 17 Jul 1943 lists gun commanders, cannoneers and ammunition men, p0560-p0564), but its own reports never name the gun: the station panels from June 1942 to June 1943 and the records of events to April 1944 have been read. 90 mm is inferred from its battalion: Battery A fired "90mm" at Algiers on 12-13 May 1943 (rg64-427180737/p0633) and Battery B had 90 mm guns from January 1943 (rg64-427181738/p0557). Before the war the 1st Bn fired 3-inch guns on the range at Camp Henlopen, Del., 6-7 Aug 1941 (Hq 1st Bn, rg64-427178735/p0358).

name: Battery D, 106th AAA AW Bn (SP)
note: Kentucky National Guard (106th CA Bn (AA), Separate, until 1943). Its battalion's dated attachments to the 45th Infantry Division are in relations.csv (etoob-45ID/p180).

name: Medical Detachment, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / 894th AAA AW Bn
note: The regiment's medical detachment: a regimental section with the Regimental HQ Battery and a section for each battalion, its men on special duty with the batteries. 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA) became the 894th AAA AW Bn; the detachment reports as the 894th's by 19 Mar 1944. Its 1942-43 reports are book-type (roll 794, parts 2-3); March-April 1943 are missing.

name: Medical Detachment, 113th Infantry
note: New Jersey National Guard, inducted 16 Sep 1940 with the 44th Infantry Division. From December 1941 on coastal defense (the reports call the regiment RCT 113). The detachment's book-type reports (roll 1690, parts 2-3) give the station of its headquarters; it also had sections with the battalions, so a man's own post may differ.

name: Company G, 113th Infantry
note: 2nd Battalion, 113th Infantry: beach patrol on the Delaware coast (Bethany and Rehoboth Beaches) in 1943, then Port Republic, N.J., Fort Dix and Camp Pickett, Va. In April 1944 the company sent 16 of its NCOs and men as overseas replacements.

name: Company B, 313th Infantry (79th Infantry Division)
note: Its reports: Crown Hill Camp, Plymouth, 11-12 June 1944; aboard ship 13 June; Sébeville (inland from Utah Beach) 14 June; the drive on Cherbourg, which fell on 26 June; then south to the Ay river and the battle for La Haye-du-Puits in July. Stations give the nearest hamlet and a grid reference on the French Lambert Zone I grid, with a distance and bearing from the grid point.

name: HQ Battery, 128th AAA Gun Bn (Mbl)
note: A 90 mm gun battalion activated at Fort Bliss, Texas, on 20 May 1943. Third Army, as an army or corps battalion, from Normandy (late June 1944) to May 1945. Its headquarters ran the SCR-584 radar and the communications net. For 1945 the positions are the battalion's symbol on Third Army's antiaircraft situation maps. Third Army's antiaircraft section's final "batting averages" (enclosure to its last weekly report, 17 May 1945, aar3/p146) credit the battalion with 17 1/4 Category I and II claims (destroyed and probably destroyed) from 146 enemy aircraft engaged, 1 Aug 1944 to 9 May 1945 (.1182, 27th of the army's battalions), and 5 1/4 from 41 since 1 Feb 1945 (.1280, 20th); claims while attached or assigned to Third Army, not final. In August 1944 it was in the 27th AAA Group under the 38th AAA Brigade (aar3/p082).

name: 9th Armored Division
note: Activated 15 Jul 1942 at Fort Riley. The positions are the division's (or a combat command's), from its 1945 G.I. Stories booklet, Third Army's after action report and other division-level sources, and are drawn as assumed.

name: Headquarters, 9th Armored Division (command post)
note: The division's command post, from the ETO order of battle's table of command posts (etoob-9AD/p503-505). A headquarters' own position: not the division's units, which were spread around it (the 60th Armored Infantry Bn at Metzeresche while the command post was at Ennery). Transcribed from 31 Jul 1944 to 6 May 1945: the whole table.

name: 60th Armored Infantry Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). The positions are the battalion's own, from its monthly after action reports, October 1944 - March 1945, as transcribed by EUCMH (eucmh60aib; original in NARA RG 407), and are drawn solid. A company's move (Able Co to Distroff, 9 Feb 1945) is not the battalion's and is not a station. Transcribed so far: October 1944 - March 1945.

name: Combat Command A, 9th Armored Division
note: A headquarters of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499) that commanded the battalions given it for an operation. Its relationships only so far (attached to the 1st Infantry Division, May 1945); its positions are in the division's rows (9ad), which name the combat command where the record does.

name: Combat Command B, 9th Armored Division
note: A headquarters of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499) that commanded the battalions given it for an operation. In December 1944 attached to V Corps, then the 106th Division and the 7th Armored at St. Vith (etoob-9AD/p501; army/relations.csv). Its positions are in the division's rows (9ad), which name the combat command where the record does.

name: Combat Command R (Reserve), 9th Armored Division
note: The 9th Armored Division's reserve command (etoob-9AD/p499), which commanded the battalions given it for an operation. Attached to the 101st Airborne Division at Bastogne, 19-31 December 1944 (etoob-9AD/p501; army/relations.csv). Its positions are in the division's rows (9ad).

name: 131st Ordnance Maintenance Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division's Trains (etoob-9AD/p499: "131st Ordnance Maintenance Battalion"). The division's third-echelon repair battalion. No stations yet: none of its own records has been found online; its position is assumed to be within the division's area, which is not a record of it.

name: 2d Tank Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). No stations yet: its own records have not been found online.

name: 14th Tank Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). No stations yet: its own records have not been found online.

name: 19th Tank Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: Part of the 9th Armored Division (etoob-9AD/p499). From October 1943 the stations are its Service Company's (19tb-serv).

name: Service Company, 19th Tank Battalion (9th Armored Division)
note: The battalion's maintenance and supply company. Formed in the division's reorganization of October 1943 from the 2nd Armored Regiment's third battalion; its morning reports are read from 11 Oct 1943 (NARA RG 64). Stations from its own reports; the battalion's companies were not always with it.

name: Headquarters, 45th Infantry Division (command post)
note: The division's command post, from the ETO order of battle's table of command posts (etoob-45ID/p184-187). A headquarters' own position: not the division's units, which were spread around it. Transcribed from 15 Aug 1944 to 1 May 1945: the whole table.

name: Headquarters & Headquarters Battery, 1st Bn, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)

name: Battery D, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)

name: Battery H, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA)

note: Its entry in the ETO order of battle begins etoob-101ABN/p381. The 9th Armored's 2d Tk Bn was attached to it 19-30 Dec 44 and its CC R 19-31 Dec 44, at Bastogne (etoob-9AD/p501). Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `101abn`).

name: 276th Volks Grenadier Division
note: German. Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-276vgd`): the map's hatched "276".

name: 352d Volks Grenadier Division
note: German. In the plan for 16 December 1944 it "would cross into the zone held by the 3d Battalion of the 109th" Infantry (28th Division), on the Our (cole/9/p213). Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-352vgd`): the map's hatched "352", and its parts as drawn ("352(-)", "352 ELMS").

name: 26th Volks Grenadier Division
note: German. In December 1944 "already was deployed in the Eifel sector of the West Wall adjacent to the Our" (cole/8/p177), then at Bastogne. Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-26vgd`): the map's hatched "26"; a "2?6" (a figure unread, perhaps the 276th) is left untied.

name: 3d Parachute Division
note: German (Fallschirmjaeger). In the attack of 16 December 1944 it formed "the left wing in the initial disposition for the attack" (cole/5/p81). Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-3fj`): the map's hatched "3" with the airborne mark, from 21 December, where it is the day's one such symbol; the other "3"s are `which-unit` (records/fronts/README.md, "The divisions tied").

name: 3d Panzer Grenadier Division
note: German. On 18 December 1944 it "marched west from reserve to take over the battle with the 2d Division" at Elsenborn (cole/6/p121); at the end of December it was sent to Bastogne (cole/24/p614). Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-3pzgr`): the map's hatched "3" with the armored mark (with or without the cross), from 21 December, where it is the day's one such symbol and not where the 3d Parachute stands; the other "3"s are `which-unit`.

name: 15th Panzer Grenadier Division
note: German. "One regimental combat team from the 15th Panzer Grenadier Division was all" Model would give for the Bastogne operation on 24 December 1944 (cole/19/p474). Followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-15pzgr`): the map's hatched "15", one symbol a day on one track (north of Aachen in December, west of Bastogne from 25 December, by St. Vith in late January, by Goch in February), whatever its mark.

name: Fuehrer Grenadier Brigade
note: German. "a younger brother of the elite Grossdeutschland Panzer Division" (cole/21/p533), it fought the 26th Division at Eschdorf (cole/21/p522) and the 80th at Heiderscheid on 24-25 December 1944 (cole/21/p541) and withdrew "during the last nights of December" into the Seventh Army's reserve at Wiltz (cole/24/p641). The map labels it "GD", as it does the Fuehrer Begleit Brigade: followed so far by its symbols on the 12th Army Group's situation maps (records/fronts/, unit `de-fgb`), the southern "GD" only, `tied-by-place` (records/fronts/README.md, "The divisions tied"), and the "FG" the maps draw with the armored mark on 10 of the read days, 28 January - 9 February 1945 (first loc-12ag/ict21238), tied by its label.

name: Fuehrer Begleit Brigade
note: German. Like the Fuehrer Grenadier Brigade, raised from the Grossdeutschland (cole/21/p533). Cole has it leave the Ourthe on 26 December 1944 and attack west of Bastogne from the 28th; with the 3d Panzer Grenadier Division it attacked Task Force Collins at Chenogne on 30 December (cole/24/p613, cole/24/p619). No symbol on the 12th Army Group's maps is tied to it yet: the northern "GD" by La Roche, 27 December - 5 January, fits neither brigade (fronts/README.md, "The divisions tied").
